output.reason: The amendment cuts the JKP contribution from 0.46% to 0.36% of wages. It is now funded only by the Central Government (0.22%) and a 0.14% recomposition of JKK. The JKM recomposition in the original PP 37/2021 is dropped, so the employer-paid JKM premium returns to its normal level, while JKK risk-class rates stay at the recomposed values. Employer-paid JKK and JKM premiums are part of a permanent employee's gross income for PPh 21. A change in the effective JKM premium therefore changes the PPh 21 base. The JKM effect is inferred, not stated: the document never mentions JKM rates directly. The new JKP benefit rules (60% of wages for 6 months) concern unemployment benefits, not monthly payroll withholding.
